questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Rose, Lotus, Lily, Mango.
questions.explanation: Rose, lotus and lily are flowers; mango is a fruit.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Apple, Banana, Carrot, Guava.
questions.explanation: Apple, banana and guava are fruits; carrot is a vegetable.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Dog, Cat, Lion, Cow.
questions.explanation: Dog, cat and cow are domestic animals; the lion is a wild animal.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Copper, Iron, Silver, Diamond.
questions.explanation: Copper, iron and silver are metals; diamond is a non-metal (a form of carbon).

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Square, Circle, Triangle, Cube.
questions.explanation: Square, circle and triangle are two-dimensional figures; a cube is a three-dimensional solid.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: January, March, May, Sunday.
questions.explanation: January, March and May are months; Sunday is a day of the week.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Cricket, Football, Hockey, Chess.
questions.explanation: Cricket, football and hockey are outdoor field sports; chess is an indoor board game.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Ganga.
questions.explanation: Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai are cities; the Ganga is a river.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 3, 5, 9, 11.
questions.explanation: 3, 5 and 11 are prime numbers; 9 = 3 × 3 is composite.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 168, 169.
questions.explanation: 121 = 11², 144 = 12², 169 = 13² are perfect squares; 168 is not a perfect square.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Triangle, Pentagon, Hexagon, Circle.
questions.explanation: Triangle, pentagon and hexagon are polygons with straight sides; a circle has no straight sides or vertices.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Lizard, Crocodile, Snake, Frog.
questions.explanation: Lizard, crocodile and snake are reptiles; the frog is an amphibian.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon.
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Earth are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Metre, Centimetre, Kilometre, Kilogram.
questions.explanation: Metre, centimetre and kilometre are units of length; the kilogram is a unit of mass.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Guitar, Flute, Violin, Sitar.
questions.explanation: Guitar, violin and sitar are stringed instruments; the flute is a wind instrument.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Cobra, Viper, Krait, Eel.
questions.explanation: Cobra, viper and krait are snakes; the eel is a fish.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: India, China, Japan, Paris.
questions.explanation: India, China and Japan are countries; Paris is a city.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Rupee, Dollar, Euro, Bank.
questions.explanation: Rupee, dollar and euro are currencies; a bank is a financial institution.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: BD, FH, JL, MO.
questions.explanation: Within each pair the letters differ by 2 (B→D, F→H, J→L, M→O). But the first letters run B(2), F(6), J(10), then should be N(14) — 'MO' starts at M(13), breaking the +4 step, so MO is the odd pair.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: AZ, BY, CX, DV.
questions.explanation: In AZ, BY, CX the two letters are symmetric from the ends of the alphabet and their position-values sum to 27 (1+26, 2+25, 3+24). DV gives 4+22 = 26, so it breaks the rule (it should be DW).

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 24, 36, 48, 50.
questions.explanation: 24, 36 and 48 are multiples of 12; 50 is not.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100.
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³ and 64 = 4³ are perfect cubes; 100 = 10² is a perfect square, not a cube.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Copper, Bronze, Brass, Steel.
questions.explanation: Bronze, brass and steel are alloys (mixtures); copper is a pure metallic element.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Radius, Diameter, Circumference, Volume.
questions.explanation: Radius, diameter and circumference are properties of a two-dimensional circle; volume is a property of a three-dimensional solid.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 343, 512, 1000, 1330.
questions.explanation: 343 = 7³, 512 = 8³ and 1000 = 10³ are perfect cubes; 1330 is not a cube (11³ = 1331).

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Trumpet, Trombone, Tuba, Cello.
questions.explanation: Trumpet, trombone and tuba are brass wind instruments; the cello is a stringed instrument.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: ACE, BDF, CEG, DGI.
questions.explanation: In ACE, BDF and CEG each letter increases by 2 (A,C,E; B,D,F; C,E,G). DGI jumps D→G (by 3), so it breaks the +2, +2 rule (it should be DFH).

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 121, 132, 143, 150.
questions.explanation: 121 (11×11), 132 (11×12) and 143 (11×13) are multiples of 11; 150 is not divisible by 11.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Square, Rhombus, Rectangle, Trapezium.
questions.explanation: A square, rhombus and rectangle are parallelograms (both pairs of opposite sides parallel); a trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Nitrogen, Oxygen, Hydrogen, Mercury.
questions.explanation: At room temperature nitrogen, oxygen and hydrogen are gases; mercury is a liquid metal.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 7, 13, 19, 25.
questions.explanation: The numbers look like an arithmetic sequence (+6), but classified by type, 7, 13 and 19 are prime while 25 = 5 × 5 is composite.

questions.stem: Find the odd one out: Almirah, Table, Chair, Wood.
questions.explanation: An almirah, table and chair are pieces of furniture; wood is the raw material from which they are made.
